title: Iterated global Weil operators evaluated at moving geometric points
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in an algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ in the rational/common-stage coefficient categories [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Let $Y_0$ be proper of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $K=(M,\theta)$ be a bounded constructible Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Write $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times h$, $P=L g^*$, $P_r=L(g^r)^*$, $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the specified scalar-localized integral pullback-composition comparisons [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. Put $C=R\Gamma_c(Y,-)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and $F=C(\theta)\circ\tau_{c,M}$, with the specified compact transport and global geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport, def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius].

For a $k$-point $z:s\to Y$ let $e_z^M:C(M)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M)$ be the canonical compact rational counit germ [def-a1-proper-sections-germ-and-moving-point, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and put $T(z)=gzh^{-1}$, $z_r=T^r(z)=g^rz h^{-r}$. For $r\geq1$, the equality $g^rz=z_rh^r$ defines the composition comparison $b_{r,z,M}:Q_rLz_r^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz^*P_rM$. Write $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P^r$ for the specified iterated comparison and define
$$\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=C(d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\tau_{c,P^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M}.$$
Use the iterated Weil map $\theta^{[r]}:P_rM\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ and iterated point transport $I_N^{[r]}:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Q_rN)$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Then, as morphisms in the derived coefficient category,
$$F^r=C(\theta^{[r]})\circ\tau^{[r]}_{c,M},$$
$$e_z^M\circ F^r=B_{r,z}\circ e_{z_r}^M,\qquad B_{r,z}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\theta^{[r]})\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})\circ I_{Lz_r^*M}^{[r]}.$$
The morphism $B_{r,z}$ is an isomorphism, natural for morphisms of Weil complexes. If $T^r(z)=z$, it is exactly the degree-$r$ local geometric-Frobenius operator with the return $g^rz=zh^r$ and the specified comparisons of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. In particular, for a geometric lift of a closed point $x$ and $r=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, whenever this return holds it is the closed-point local operator. The formulas are at the derived level before taking any cohomology. At $\Qlb$ they are the scalar extensions of the same formulas at a common finite field stage. No invariant integral lattice, weight, semisimplicity, or finiteness of $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is assumed.

The functors $C$, $\operatorname{Fib}_{z}$, contracted transports $\tau^{[r]}$, moving-point identities, comparisons $b_{r,z,M}$ and finite-stage realizations are the specified constructions of [def-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-iterate-data]. At $\Qlb$, the cohomology functor and its canonical source identification are those of [def-a1-common-stage-cohomology-realization]; the point Frobenius and coefficient inclusions and finite index fields are those of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].

source.place: (1.1.3), p.150; (1.1.7), pp.150-151; (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), pp.151-153. Agent extraction of the explicit naturality induction and germ calculation in steps 4-6 of lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition, using the specified semilinear germ identity rather than asserting equality with an unspecified Frobenius transport.

proof.text: Put $t=\tau_{c,-}:C\Rightarrow CP$, natural by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]; properness includes separatedness, so its hypotheses hold. Apply [lem-trf-global-frobenius-iterate-formula] with $G=P$ and structure map $\theta$. Writing $\widehat\theta_r=\theta\circ P(\theta)\circ\cdots\circ P^{r-1}(\theta)$ and $\widehat\tau_r=t_{P^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ t_M$, it gives $F^r=C(\widehat\theta_r)\widehat\tau_r$. The iterate in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is $\theta^{[r]}=\widehat\theta_r d_{r,M}$: both are the same ordered list of pulled-back copies of $\theta$, with brackets identified by the associative comparisons of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] and their specified scalar localizations. Thus $C(\widehat\theta_r)=C(\theta^{[r]})C(d_{r,M}^{-1})$, proving the first formula with exactly the stated $\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}$.

source.place: (1.1.10), p.151, action of the Weil generator; (1.1.14), p.153, cohomology operator. Explicit categorical iteration.

proof.text: The germ of [def-a1-proper-sections-germ-and-moving-point] is natural in the underlying complex, not only in Weil morphisms. Indeed write $R=Ra_{Y*}$ and $v_z^M=Lz^*(\varepsilon_M)u_z(RM)^{-1}$, where $u_z:Lz^*La_Y^*\cong\mathrm{id}$. Naturality of the counit of [fix-prop-adjunctions] and of $u_z$ from [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] gives $Lz^*(f)v_z^M=v_z^N R(f)$ for $f:M\to N$. Apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and the natural proper comparison of [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius]. With the scalar-localized germ specified in the definition this reads $e_z^N C(f)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*f)e_z^M$.

source.place: (1.1.3), p.150, scalar localization; (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), pp.151-153, transport of fibres. Naturality of the specified counit germ.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-germs] to $M$, at the same coefficient stage. Its properness, bounded constructibility, $k$-point and specified-comparison hypotheses are precisely ours. It gives $z_r=g^rzh^{-r}$ as a $k$-point and $e_z^{P_rM}\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})I_{Lz_r^*M}^{[r]}e_{z_r}^M$. Use step 2 with $f=\theta^{[r]}:P_rM\to M$ and then step 1. The result is
$$e_z^MF^r=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\theta^{[r]})e_z^{P_rM}\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=B_{r,z}e_{z_r}^M.$$
The source of $B_{r,z}$ is $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz_r^*M)$ and its target is $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M)$, so no fixed-point assertion is used here.

source.place: (1.1.7), pp.150-151, fibre transport; (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), pp.151-153. Substitution of the specified semilinear germ identity.

proof.text: Each factor of $B_{r,z}$ is invertible. The pulled-back $\theta^{[r]}$ is invertible because the Weil structure of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is an isomorphism and functors preserve its inverse. The comparison $b_{r,z,M}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-germs]. By [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso](1) every one-step point transport is invertible; its finite composite, followed by the invertible composition comparison, is $I^{[r]}$. Composing the inverses in reverse order supplies the inverse of $B_{r,z}$.

source.place: (1.1.10), p.151, Weil action by isomorphisms; (1.1.7), pp.150-151, point transport.

proof.text:
Let $f:(M,\theta_M)\to(N,\theta_N)$ be a Weil morphism, so $f\theta_M=\theta_NP(f)$ by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. In the uncontracted iterates, induction gives $f\widehat\theta_{M,r}=\widehat\theta_{N,r}P^r(f)$: the case $r=1$ is this equation, and the successor follows by composing with $P^r(\theta_M)$ and using $P^r(f\theta_M)=P^r(\theta_NP(f))$. Naturality of $d_r$ from [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] contracts this to $f\theta_M^{[r]}=\theta_N^{[r]}P_r(f)$. The same node makes $b_{r,z}$ natural. Each point transport is natural by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), so composing its $r$ naturality squares and the composition comparison gives naturality of $I^{[r]}$. Consequently, for $U_z=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*f)$,
$$U_zB_{r,z,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\theta_N^{[r]})\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*P_r(f))\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})I^{[r]}=B_{r,z,N}U_{z_r}.$$
This proves the required naturality, including noninvertible $f$.

source.place: (1.1.10)-(1.1.13), pp.151-152, equivariant morphisms and fibre transport. Explicit naturality squares.

proof.text: If $T^r(z)=z$, substitute this equality in $g^rz=z_rh^r$. It gives $g^rz=zh^r$, and the three factors defining $B_{r,z}$ are, in order, the iterated point transport, the specified comparison for this return, and the pulled-back $\theta^{[r]}$. This is word for word the definition of the degree-$r$ local operator in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. For a lift of a closed point $x$ and $r=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, its closed-point clause uses the identical composite. Thus, whenever the stated return holds, this is the closed-point operator; no equality $g^rz=z$ of scheme morphisms is asserted. All equations so far are equations of derived morphisms, so taking cohomology is optional.

source.place: (1.1.8), p.151, and (1.1.13), p.152, degree-normalized local geometric Frobenius.

proof.text: At $\Qlb$, choose one common finite field stage for the underlying objects, $\theta$, $\theta^{-1}$ and their inverse equations, using [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the finite list of equations for a morphism $f$ can be included when proving naturality. There $\theta$ is an actual rational isomorphism. All operations and the unit, counit and exchange comparisons commute with scalar extension by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], and point transport does so by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2). The germ formula of [lem-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-germs] is already stated with these common-stage factors. Hence the equations above at that stage represent exactly the asserted $\Qlb$ equations; equality and composition of their classes are defined at a common finite stage. No step reduces $\theta$ to an invertible integral map. Neither weights, semisimplicity nor finiteness of the proper structure morphism has been used.

Specified associative natural pullback comparisons, already statement dependencies; no duality theorem is used.

Naturality and finite coefficient-extension compatibility of the specified point transport are needed for B and its common-stage realization.
Only rationalization/common-stage compatibility of operations, units, counits and exchange transformations is used.
